text:
According to an old legend, a clever courtier once invented a new game and presented it to his king. The king loved it so much that he offered the inventor any reward he wished.

“Your Majesty,” said the courtier humbly, “I ask for something very small. Place one grain of rice on the first square of the chessboard, two on the second, four on the third, and continue doubling for each of the sixty-four squares.”

The king laughed. “Is that all? A man of your talent could have asked for gold or land!” He ordered his servants to prepare the rice.

At first, the numbers looked trivial. By the tenth square, there were only five hundred grains. By the twentieth, about half a million, still just a few sacks. The king was amused.

But by the thirtieth square, the amount had grown to over a billion grains. By the fortieth, it filled granaries. By the sixty-fourth, the total was so large that no kingdom on earth could have provided it. It was more than all the rice ever grown in history.

The king fell silent. He had not understood how quickly small, steady increases could accumulate when they multiplied. He had underestimated the power of exponential growth.

He admired the courtier’s intelligence, and appointed him chief advisor, instead of demanding the impossible reward.

Moral: Small things that grow steadily can become unimaginably powerful.

quiz.q: The courtier asked for one grain of rice on the first square.
The king could easily give the full reward.
What happened to the rice on each new square?
What did the king do instead of giving the reward?
o: He made the courtier chief advisor
